title: Finite diagrams of finite etale covers have local finite-set normal forms
statement:
Let $Y$ be a scheme and let $D:\mathcal I\to\mathsf{FEt}(Y)$ be a diagram of finite etale $Y$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category], indexed by a finite category $\mathcal I$ [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits]. There is a set-indexed family of etale maps $u_\lambda:U_\lambda\to Y$ whose images cover $Y$, and for each $\lambda$ a functor $S_\lambda:\mathcal I\to\mathbf{Set}$ with finite values, together with isomorphisms of $U_\lambda$-schemes
$$e_{\lambda,i}:D(i)\times_YU_\lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}\coprod_{s\in S_\lambda(i)}U_\lambda$$
for every object $i$ (scheme coproducts as in [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]), such that for every arrow $f:i\to j$, the conjugate $e_{\lambda,j}\circ D(f)_{U_\lambda}\circ e_{\lambda,i}^{-1}$ sends the summand indexed by $s$ identically to the summand indexed by $S_\lambda(f)(s)$. The finite sets may depend on $\lambda$; no constant degree over all of $Y$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0BN9, lemma-finite-etale-covers-limits-colimits, finite colimits proof: simultaneous splitting and further open refinement of index maps; finite-diagram generalization of the parallel-pair argument

proof.text: If $Y$ is empty, take the empty covering family. Otherwise enumerate the objects of the finite category as $i_1,\ldots,i_n$. We construct, by induction on $k$, a set-indexed etale covering family of $Y$ on whose members the first $k$ objects are finite coproducts of the base. For $k=0$, use $\mathrm{id}_Y$ and no trivializations. Base changes of $D(i)$ remain finite etale by the base change functor in [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category].

source.place: Tag 0BN9, lemma-finite-etale-covers-limits-colimits, finite colimits proof, simultaneous splitting and further open refinement; finite-diagram extension

proof.text: Suppose the family at stage $k$ is constructed, and let $W\to Y$ be one member. At every $w\in W$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-etale-local-split] to $D(i_{k+1})\times_YW\to W$. It gives $V_w\to W$ etale, a point above $w$, and a finite disjoint union of pieces each isomorphic over $V_w$ to $V_w$. For each piece $Z_a$, let $q_a:Z_a\xrightarrow{\sim}V_w$ be its structural isomorphism. The coproduct universal property constructs $e:\coprod_a Z_a\to\coprod_a V_w$ with components $\iota_a\circ q_a$ and its inverse with components $\kappa_a\circ q_a^{-1}$. Their composites restrict to the identity on every summand, so uniqueness proves they are inverse. Since each $q_a$ is the structural morphism, this is an isomorphism over $V_w$, giving the next trivialization. The maps $V_w\to Y$ are etale by composition. Pull back the earlier trivializations; [lem-sc-etale-fibre-product-base-change-coproduct] identifies each pulled-back finite coproduct with copies of $V_w$, preserving its labels and projections. Iterated fibre products identify the pulled-back objects with $D(i)\times_YV_w$: both have the same compatible-map universal property. The new members cover every $W$, because one lies above each $w$, hence still cover $Y$. Finite induction gives the desired objectwise trivializations $e_i$ over each member $W$, with finite index sets $S(i)$ that may depend on $W$.

source.place: Tag 0BN9, lemma-finite-etale-covers-limits-colimits, finite colimits proof, simultaneous splitting and further open refinement; finite-diagram extension

proof.text: Fix such a member $W$. For every arrow $f:i\to j$, conjugate its base change by $e_i,e_j$, obtaining $h_f:\coprod_{s\in S(i)}W\to\coprod_{t\in S(j)}W$ over $W$. Restrict to a source summand $s$ and apply [lem-galois-coproduct-copies-morphisms-clopen](a). It gives a clopen decomposition $(W_{f,s,t})_{t\in S(j)}$ of $W$, and on $W_{f,s,t}$ the restriction is precisely the inclusion of summand $t$ composed with the structural inclusion $W_{f,s,t}\to W$. There are only finitely many pairs $(f,s)$, because there are finitely many arrows and each $S(i)$ is finite.

source.place: Tag 03YW, example-constant-group, functor of points of a disjoint union of base copies; used for the open refinement in Tag 0BN9

proof.text: For each $w\in W$ and pair $(f,s)$, let $t_w(f,s)$ be the unique label with $w\in W_{f,s,t_w(f,s)}$. Put $V_w=\bigcap_{(f,s)}W_{f,s,t_w(f,s)}$; the empty intersection is $W$. This is open, contains $w$, and the $V_w$ cover $W$. The composite $V_w\to W\to Y$ is etale since an open immersion is etale and etale maps compose. Restrict the $e_i$ to $V_w$, using finite-coproduct base change. By the restriction equations of [lem-galois-coproduct-copies-morphisms-clopen](a), $h_f$ now carries summand $s$ identically into summand $t_w(f,s)$. Define $S_w(f)(s)=t_w(f,s)$ and $S_w(i)=S(i)$. The functor laws hold: the conjugate of an identity is an identity, and $h_{g\circ f}=h_g\circ h_f$ by cancellation of $e_j^{-1}e_j$. Evaluate these equalities on the point $w$ of each source summand. Disjointness of target summands forces $S_w(\mathrm{id})(s)=s$ and $S_w(g\circ f)(s)=S_w(g)(S_w(f)(s))$. If the source index set is empty these equations are vacuous. A nonempty source cannot have empty target index set, since the corresponding clopen decomposition of the nonempty $V_w$ would have no pieces. Thus all functions and all functor laws, including the empty-index cases, are defined.

source.place: Tag 0BN9, lemma-finite-etale-covers-limits-colimits, finite colimits proof, simultaneous splitting and further open refinement; finite-diagram extension

proof.text: Index the final family by pairs consisting of a member $W$ at stage $n$ and a point $w\in W$. All these indices form a set: each induction stage uses a set-indexed union of sets of points, and there are finitely many stages. The resulting $U_\lambda=V_w$ cover $Y$, since the $W$ cover $Y$ and the $V_w$ cover each $W$. Take $S_\lambda=S_w$ and the restricted trivializations as $e_{\lambda,i}$. The displayed restriction equations are exactly the required clause for every arrow. When the diagram is empty the same construction has no object or arrow data and still yields a covering. No stage identifies sheet counts on different members.

Step 4: t_w exists because an empty target index set would force W to be empty; V_w is open, contains w and is etale over Y; the identity and composition laws follow by evaluating on the nonempty V_w with disjoint summands.
